title: Bangla Book Recommendation
description: A graph-based recommendation system for Bangla literature, enabling more accurate and personalized book discovery.
details: Developed using a multi-entity book graph dataset to power advanced recommendation models. Focuses on improving user experience through intelligent personalization. Dataset: https://github.com/backlashblitz/Bangla-Book-Recommendation-Dataset

title: Brazilian E-Commerce Data Warehouse & Analytics Project
description: A modern data warehouse built with SQL Server, featuring T-SQL & SSIS ETL pipelines, automated job scheduling, and a Power BI analytics layer.
details: End-to-end data warehousing solution following Medallion Architecture (Bronze, Silver, Gold layers), built on the Brazilian E-Commerce (Olist) dataset. Ingests raw ERP and CRM data from CSV sources, cleanses and normalizes it in the Silver layer, and models it into a star schema in the Gold layer. Includes a parallel SSIS implementation (Bronze/Silver/Master control flow packages) deployed on Azure-SSIS Integration Runtime, a SQL Server Agent job for automated daily scheduling, and both Power BI and Tableau dashboards covering revenue, order/review analytics, product performance, and regional breakdowns.

title: LenDen Online Mobile Banking
description: A web-based mobile banking application enabling secure account management, fund transfers, and transaction tracking.
details: Built with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript (React.js) on the frontend, PHP and MySQL (XAMPP) on the backend, with session-based authentication and optional JWT support.

title: Object Detection with SSL & Semi-Supervised Learning

title: Real-time Chat App

details: Full-stack app using Node.js, Socket.io, and a minimalist frontend.

title: Brazilian E-Commerce Review Sentiment Analysis
description: Binary sentiment classification of Olist customer reviews, benchmarking 45+ model runs across classical, transformer, and deep-learning families to power a customer-service triage tool.
details: Classifies 33,471 labeled Olist reviews as positive/negative, comparing three published approaches: classical ML (9 classifiers × 4 vectorizers), fine-tuned transformers (BERTimbau, XLM-R, m-BERT, DistilBERT-multilingual), and deep sequence models (LSTM/BiLSTM/CNN-LSTM/CNN-BiLSTM with Portuguese fastText embeddings). Fine-tuned BERTimbau won overall (F1 0.9471), while a simple count-bigram + SGD classifier came within striking distance (F1 0.9350) at a fraction of the cost. The best classical model is deployed against the full review dataset to build a negative-review priority queue for CS agents and a category/seller sentiment trend dashboard, with data-leakage safeguards (deduplication, train-only fitting, held-out test isolation) baked into the pipeline. Built on top of a companion medallion-architecture data warehouse project.
